methodology.method_family: institutional case description and policy forum
methodology.study_design: institutional experience report with planned/ongoing proof-of-concept activities
methodology.sample_description: PMDA internal operations, policies, and initiatives across regulatory reviews, safety measures, and relief services
methodology.sector: pharmaceutical and medical device regulatory agency
methodology.technology_context: commercially available generative artificial intelligence tools for administrative support and exploration of large language models in secure internal environments for scientifically specialized tasks

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article provides substantive evidence on generative AI and LLM governance, human-in-the-loop oversight, information governance, and regulated institutional adoption at PMDA. However, the supplied text contains no explicit focus on conversational AI, chatbots, agents, or conversational governance mechanisms, so it is better classified as supporting rather than central evidence for a review on conversational governance in LLM-based systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Provided text is truncated after page 2; metadata extraction was corrupted; conversational AI relevance is absent in available excerpts and requires full-text confirmation.

appraisal.notes: Policy forum-style institutional account with clear governance framing but limited transparent empirical methodology in the provided text; suitability is descriptive rather than evaluative.

cerqual.explanation: The governance narrative is coherent and institutionally grounded, but available text offers incomplete methodological detail and no conversational-system focus, limiting confidence for central synthesis on conversational governance.

coding.theme: Institutional governance for generative AI and LLM adoption in a regulated health agency
coding.subtheme: Phased deployment with human oversight and information governance
rq_alignment: governance of generative AI in regulated environments

synthesis.main_claim: PMDA is proactively but cautiously adopting generative AI and exploring LLMs through a governance-centered phased strategy that preserves human judgment, strengthens information governance, and supports regulatory work without replacing expert oversight.
synthesis.contribution: Offers an institutional governance framework and implementation strategy from a national medicines regulator, combining commercial GenAI for administrative tasks with secure internal LLM exploration for specialized scientific work.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text is partial; no explicit conversational AI governance content; empirical evaluation details, limitations section, and operational controls such as audit, tracing, or contestation are not evidenced in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on regulated institutional GenAI/LLM governance, human-in-the-loop oversight, and phased adoption in healthcare regulation; not as primary evidence for conversational governance mechanisms.
